top_choice_rationale: P002 credits a discovery or invention and the people responsible with the least attribution strain: Katori's magic-wavelength optical lattice clock (concept and first realisation) and Ye's development of it to about 10^-18, reproduced independently at several national laboratories. The magic-wavelength condition lets thousands of neutral atoms be interrogated free of Doppler, recoil and trap-induced shifts, a different architecture from the frequency comb (2005) and single-ion control (2012), so a citation naming the lattice and magic wavelength claims neither lineage. P001 is scientifically mature and a close second, but it leaves the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang step outside the three names, and Zhang's death means this cannot be repaired later. P003 is a clean prediction-plus-observation pairing, but the experimental credit rests on Jarillo-Herrero alone with Cao and others outside the names, and the decisive work is only seven to eight years old. P000 is last because at least two proposals are mature and defensible.
recusal_note: No collaboration or supervisory tie to Katori or Ye is apparent from the profile, but a University of Tokyo fellowship, a JSPS fellowship and long-running exchanges with Japanese universities (Katori is at the University of Tokyo) are an institutional connection to record. Separately, my field is electron microscopy, so I could not claim independence on B012, which is not in this slate.
